scope: Proposition 4.6 (The quartic homogeneous obstruction) of the manuscript “Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-Torus-Packets-for-Arbitrary-Orders-October-5-2026/quartic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95c2a937da74097a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ν be an A4-invariant, A4-ergodic probability on X4. Suppose that hν(a0(1)) > 0 for some one-parameter subgroup a0 : R → A4. Then either ν = m4, or there exists b ∈ B such that ν(Eb) = 1. In the latter case every lattice Λ′ in the homogeneous orbit carrying ν has a vector in V2 Λ′ ∩ Vb with both coordinates nonzero and with nonzero integer Q-value.
